Persistent neural states

Persistent activity as a memory mechanism

A mathematical neural model explored conditions under which patterns of activity could persist.

W. A. Little

AI topics

Explore related entries. Larger tags appear on more entries.

MemoryPersistent statesNeural networksRecurrent networks

The contribution

Little studied when a neural network could sustain ordered states despite the changing activity of its individual units. He connected this behavior to an analogy with interacting spins and proposed a relationship between persistent states and short-term memory. The work provided a precursor to later treatments of memory through collective network dynamics.

What this does not establish

Persistent state here refers to activity in a mathematical neural model. It is not disk storage, an always-running software agent, or a complete biological explanation of memory.

Why this date?

The original article was published in 1974. Hopfield cites its author, year, journal, volume, and page range as reference 8.
